92:### Two-Phase Handoff
95:QEMU1 --(state file + shared mmap)--> vsim (resume + run ROI + drain)
103:**CSR restore split**: `ResumeDriver` writes the CSRs the vsim phase can touch: `mstatus`, `mtvec`, `mscratch` (L23), `mepc`/`mcause`/`mtval`/`mie`/`mip` (L24), `mcycle`, `minstret`, `fcsr` (frm + sticky fflags, gated on `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`; L20), and the Andes machine-setup CSRs `mcache_ctl` (0x7CA) + `mmisc_ctl` (0x7D0) (L21). The cache pair matters for the cycle figure, not correctness: crt0 enables the L1 I/D caches via `mcache_ctl`, but that write runs on the cache-less functional engine, so without transporting it vsim resumes at the ROI with caches at their reset default (disabled) and the whole window runs uncached -- inflating the cycle count severalfold. All are tolerant writes: an engine without a given custom CSR mirrors the write as a no-op. In the trap-free ROI these writable M-mode CSRs are ordinary read/write state, so they round-trip fully: restored at resume, re-read at drain (`StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough`), and compared by `--verify` (`state_diff`). Two verify-side exceptions: `mip` is restored + re-read but NOT compared -- its pending bits are hardware/platform-driven (the timer bit tracks elapsed time, which advances differently in QEMU's functional clock vs vsim's cycle clock), so comparing it would false-positive; and `mtvec` is restored but not re-drained. The QEMU plugin still drains `medeleg`/`mideleg`/`satp` into `hybrid_state_v1`, but those are S-mode CSRs the default M-only engine (`ax45mpv_premium`, `NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1`) does not implement, so they are not restored -- they remain in `hybrid_state_v1` only as the drained record, deferred to the S/U-envelope work. The vsim phase is assumed trap-free, interrupt-free, and PMP-static; if a future workload needs traps or dynamic PMP inside the ROI, `ResumeDriver` must be extended.
105:**Privilege (L6)**: the handoff carries the real privilege level. The plugin drains the gdbstub `priv` register, `ResumeDriver` read-modify-writes `dcsr.prv` before `dret` (and verifies the write took -- an M-mode-only RTL like the default `ax45mpv_premium`, `NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1`, WARL-pins the field, and the resume aborts with a pick-an-S/U-capable-engine error), and `StateDrain` reads `dcsr.prv` back at the exit halt. For S/U handoffs the producer's PMP block (64 `pmpaddr` + the 8 even `pmpcfg`) is also mirrored into the hart, because with PMP implemented and no matching entry every S/U access faults; M-mode handoffs keep PMP pass-through-only (L2). The `rt_priv_smode`/`rt_priv_umode` fixtures run on the S/U-capable `ax66_makatau` engine paired with QEMU `-cpu andes-ax66` (see `scripts/run_e2e.sh`); the ROI itself must still be trap-free, single-privilege, and paging-off (S-mode CSRs are not transported).
114:- **marker mode** (default): Pattern-matches `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0` (entry) / `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1` (exit) at retire time. The markers are RISC-V HINTs (rd=x0 discards the result), i.e. architectural NOPs -- a marker binary also runs standalone on every engine and on silicon. Users get them from `<andesim/ROI.h>` (`andesim_ROI_begin()/end()`).
118:- **icount mode**: single boundary on each leg - plugin `icount=N` fast-forwards QEMU1, vsim `--hybrid-icount M` measures the window and drains. No markers, no warmup; for marker-less workloads. Removed as an `andesim --trigger` option; the measurement mechanism (plan `Trigger{kind:"icount"}` -> plugin `icount=` / vsim `--hybrid-icount`) is retained for SimPoint and driven directly by `./hsim.py run --mode icount`.
119:- **SimPoint-driven mode**: profile the run into slices (interval = insns per slice), cluster representative phases, measure each phase like icount, weight-combine into a whole-program cycle estimate. Drive via `./hsim.py run --mode simpoint` (or the equivalent `./hsim.py estimate`) -- Python golden only until the C++ port lands. The bbv-profile / archive / replay machinery are its stages, not separate modes.
121:`./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker|pc` is the unified orchestrator for the kernel modes (`./hsim.py run --mode icount|simpoint` for the whole-program modes); `tests/e2e.sh` drives marker/pc internally. Each yields a cycle figure: kernel/window cycles = the vsim `mcycle` delta (`hybrid_state_v1::mcycle`); SimPoint reports the weight-combined `estimated_cycles`.
186:Fixture source lives in `tests/fixtures/`; the shared runtime sources live at the repo root in `runtime/`. ALL C fixtures (rt_c_* and vplat_*) link through the shipped vplat runtime with the user command (`-B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`); nothing in-tree links `-lgloss_vh` or uses semihosting syscalls anymore (asm fixtures still carry a semihosting exit fallback from `semihost_exit.inc`). V-using fixtures require `-march=rv64gcv`. Syscalls bottom out in MMIO devices both engines model (UART2 `0xf0300000`, SimControl/HTIF `0xe0080000` -- QEMU side is `QEMU/hw/misc/andes_sim_control.c`), so a `printf` inside the ROI works on every engine (it just adds the real UART cycles to the figure); the old "Phase-2 no-syscall rule" survives only as a measurement-hygiene convention in cycle-measuring fixtures, and as a hard rule for user binaries that still link a semihosting libgloss. The ROI markers are HINT NOPs, so vplat binaries may carry them (`<andesim/ROI.h>`, installed to `build/runtime/include/`) and still run standalone on every engine; binaries you cannot edit delimit the ROI with PC symbols and `--trigger pc` instead.

1	# Hybrid Simulator - Functional Requirements Specification
2	
3	Status: draft v0.1. Written 2026-05-29. Owner: Nick.
4	Audience: Engineering, QA, IP/Legal, Sales engineering.
5	
6	Companion to `MRD.md` (commercial product view). This document is
7	the **engineering contract**: every shippable behavior of Andes
8	HybridSim v1.0, with one-line acceptance criteria per requirement.
9	
10	Requirement IDs are stable across drafts. Each FR traces back to
11	one or more MR-x in MRD.md.
12	
13	---
14	
15	## 1. Scope and Definitions
16	
17	### 1.1 In scope
18	
19	Andes HybridSim v1.0, the commercial Tier-2 hybrid simulator
20	described in `MRD.md` sections 1-2. Specifically:
21	
22	- `hsim` driver CLI
23	- QEMU (Andes fork) with hybrid plugin
24	- vsim cycle engine (Verilator-derived, encrypted)
25	- State transport library (`hybrid_state_v1`)
26	- Trigger toolkit (magic-CSR, PC-watch, icount, SimPoint)
27	- Pipeline trace converter (kanata, Clarity DB)
28	- License daemon
29	- Installer, documentation, sample workloads
30	
31	### 1.2 Out of scope (v1.0)
32	
33	- Non-Andes RISC-V ISA variants
34	- QEMU + Alioth (cycle-side Alioth) - documented as future in MRD
35	- FPGA backend
36	- Cloud-hosted SaaS delivery
37	- Multi-cluster cache coherence beyond a single Andes cluster
38	- Vector extension `V` beyond what AndeStar V5 covers
39	
40	### 1.3 Definitions
41	
42	| Term | Definition |
43	|---|---|
44	| ROI | Region of Interest. Window of dynamic instructions to measure cycle-exactly. |
45	| Fast engine | QEMU 9.x with Andes plugin. Runs non-ROI code. |
46	| Cycle engine | vsim, encrypted Verilator-derived binary. Runs ROI. |
47	| Handoff | Atomic state transfer between fast and cycle engine. |
48	| Trigger | A mechanism that fires the handoff (magic-CSR write, PC match, icount expiry, SimPoint marker). |
49	| Hybrid state | `hybrid_state_v1` wire format - GPR, FPR, V-state, CSR, PC, mem snapshot, timing baseline. |
50	| Cycle figure | The cycle count delta across the ROI window, returned to the user. |
51	| Warmup | Initial cycles after handoff where cache/predictor state is not yet steady; excluded from acceptance comparison. |
52	
53	### 1.4 Traceability
54	
55	Every FR includes a `Traces: MR-x [, MR-y...]` line tying it back
56	to `MRD.md`.
57	
58	---
59	
60	## 2. System Architecture Overview
61	
62	```
63	+--------+   trigger   +----------+   handoff   +--------+
64	|  ELF   | ----------> |   QEMU   | ----------> |  vsim  |
65	| (cust) |             |  + plug  |  state +    | cycle  |
66	+--------+             +----------+   mem mmap  | engine |
67	                                                +--------+
68	                                                    |
69	                                                    v
70	                                        state + cycle count (drain)
71	```
72	
73	Two phases per workload:
74	1. **QEMU1**: boot + setup, fast.
75	2. **vsim**: ROI, cycle-exact, encrypted; drains the final state.
76	
77	Shared substrate: `/dev/shm` mmap-backed RAM, file-descriptor
78	based state transport (`hybrid_state_v1`), license daemon over
79	network socket.
80	
81	---
82	
83	## 3. FR-1xx Functional Capabilities
84	
85	### FR-101 - Two-phase handoff orchestration
86	
87	`hsim run` shall execute the QEMU1 -> vsim sequence
88	without user intervention beyond the initial invocation.
89	
90	- Inputs: ELF, ROI specification (trigger config), workload args
91	- Output: cycle figure (decimal), exit code, optional pipeline trace
92	- Acceptance: a bare-metal kernel with PC-trigger round-trips end-to-end with exit code 0.
93	- Traces: MR-A, MR-G
94	
95	### FR-102 - Trigger: magic-CSR write
96	
97	A write to a configured CSR (default `0x7C0`, customer-configurable)
98	shall fire the QEMU->vsim handoff at the next instruction boundary.
99	
100	- Acceptance: ELF that writes magic-CSR triggers handoff within 1 instruction; no false positives in 1B-cycle stress test.
101	- Traces: MR-A
102	
103	### FR-103 - Trigger: PC watchpoint
104	
105	A configured PC address shall fire the handoff at the matching
106	instruction without requiring source modification.
107	
108	- Acceptance: closed-source ELF (no magic-CSR access) triggers correctly on PC match.
109	- Traces: MR-A, MR-D (closed-source customer ELFs)
110	
111	### FR-104 - Trigger: instruction count
112	
113	A configured icount threshold shall fire the handoff after N
114	dynamic instructions from a reference point.
115	
116	- Acceptance: handoff fires at exactly icount=N, deterministic across runs.
117	- Traces: MR-C, MR-I
118	
119	### FR-105 - Trigger: SimPoint cluster marker
120	
121	The SimPoint clustering tool shall generate a per-cluster trigger
122	spec consumable by `hsim run --mode simpoint`.
123	
124	- Acceptance: SimPoint output drives N handoffs at N cluster boundaries; per-cluster cycle figures collected and weight-combined.
125	- Traces: MR-C
126	
127	### FR-106 - QEMU1 -> vsim handoff: full state transport
128	
129	The following state shall transport bit-exactly from QEMU to vsim:
130	
131	- 32 GPRs (RV64I)
132	- 32 FPRs (with NaN-boxing per RISC-V spec)
133	- V-state (vector regs + vcsr per AndeStar V5)
134	- All architectural CSRs reachable in supported privilege modes
135	- All Andes-vendor CSRs in the customer-visible list (see FR-401)
136	- PC
137	- Memory snapshot (shared mmap RAM)
138	- PMP config (read-only, enforced at vsim entry)
139	- Trap delegation state
140	
141	- Acceptance: post-handoff vsim execution of `nop` produces identical architectural-visible state as a fully-RTL run from the same checkpoint.
142	- Traces: MR-A, MR-E, MR-I
143	
144	### FR-107 - vsim -> QEMU2 handback [REMOVED 2026-06-09]
145	
146	Removed: the vsim -> QEMU2 handback leg was deleted repo-wide; the simulator is now 2-phase (QEMU1 drain -> vsim drain).
147	
148	Symmetric to FR-106. State at vsim ROI exit shall be re-injected
149	into QEMU2 bit-exactly.
150	
151	- Acceptance: bare-metal workload completes execution under QEMU2 after a vsim ROI window; final result matches fully-RTL baseline.
152	- Traces: MR-A, MR-G
153	
154	### FR-108 - M-mode workload support
155	
156	The v1.0 envelope shall include any RV64GC + AndeStar V5 workload
157	running entirely in M-mode with PMP-static, trap-free ROI.
158	
159	- Acceptance: 10 representative M-mode kernels round-trip without error.
160	- Traces: MR-A
161	
162	### FR-109 - S-mode and U-mode workload support
163	
164	The v1.0 envelope shall extend to S-mode and U-mode workloads,
165	including supervisor page tables (Sv39/Sv48) and trap handling
166	inside the ROI.
167	
168	- Acceptance: 3 Linux userspace workloads (SPEC-class) round-trip.
169	- Traces: MR-B
170	
171	### FR-110 - Cycle figure reporting
172	
173	After every successful run, `hsim` shall emit:
174	- Total ROI cycles (decimal)
175	- Per-phase wall-clock time
176	- SimPoint weighted estimate (when applicable)
177	- Confidence band on the estimate (95% CI)
178	
179	- Acceptance: machine-parseable JSON report at `hsim.report.json`.
180	- Traces: MR-C, MR-J
181	
182	### FR-111 - Pipeline trace export: kanata
183	
184	When `--trace kanata` is set, the cycle engine shall emit kanata
185	format for the ROI window, byte-identical to a fully-RTL baseline
186	after warmup.
187	
188	- Acceptance: `diff` against fully-RTL kanata is empty for the post-warmup window.
189	- Traces: MR-F
190	
191	### FR-112 - Pipeline trace export: Clarity DB
192	
193	When `--trace clarity` is set, the cycle engine shall emit a
194	Clarity-format pipeline DB for the ROI window.
195	
196	- Acceptance: Clarity DB import into the Andes Clarity viewer succeeds; per-stage event counts match fully-RTL.
197	- Traces: MR-F
198	
199	### FR-113 - Multi-hart ROI
200	
201	`hsim` shall support ROIs that span >= 4 harts with coherent state
202	transport through ACE.
203	
204	- Acceptance: a 4-hart kernel round-trips; cycle figure within 1% of fully-RTL baseline.
205	- Traces: MR-H
206	
207	### FR-114 - Resumable / checkpointed runs
208	
209	A long QEMU1 phase shall be checkpointable mid-run, so a customer
210	can boot once and re-enter vsim multiple times without re-booting.
211	
212	- Acceptance: customer boots Linux once (~30 min), then runs 10
213	  different ROIs measured against the same checkpoint, with total
214	  wall-clock under 1 hour.
215	- Traces: MR-G

219	## 4. FR-2xx Performance Requirements
220	
221	### FR-201 - Wall-clock speedup envelope
222	
223	On a workload where the ROI is <= 1% of dynamic instructions,
224	HybridSim shall complete in <= 1% of the wall-clock time of a
225	vsim-alone run of the same workload.
226	
227	- Acceptance: 3 reference workloads measured; speedup >= 100x.
228	- Traces: MR-A, MRD section 9.1
229	
230	### FR-202 - Per-ROI accuracy
231	
232	The cycle figure for the ROI window shall agree with a fully-RTL
233	baseline within 1% after a documented warmup tolerance.
234	
235	- Acceptance: 5 reference ROIs; max error <= 1.0%.
236	- Traces: MR-A, MR-E
237	
238	### FR-203 - SimPoint whole-program accuracy
239	
240	The weighted whole-program estimate from SimPoint mode shall be
241	within 5-10% of fully-RTL on SPEC-class workloads.
242	
243	- Acceptance: 3 SPEC-class workloads; max error <= 10%, average <= 5%.

252	- Acceptance: timed user study with 3 fresh engineers; 100% reach valid figure within 8 hours.

257	After an initial QEMU1 phase, a re-measurement of the same ROI

267	### FR-301 - `hsim` CLI

269	Top-level entry. Subcommands:
270	- `hsim run` - one-shot workload execution

286	- Acceptance: bad config produces actionable error pointing at the offending line.

291	Every run shall emit `hsim.report.json` with the schema defined in

294	- Acceptance: schema validation passes on every successful run.

1	# Hybrid Simulator - Market Requirements Document
2	
3	Status: draft v1.0 (commercial rewrite). Written 2026-05-29.
4	Owner: Nick. Audience: PM, BU lead, Sales engineering, Legal.
5	
6	Companion docs:
7	- `FRS.md` - functional requirements specification (engineering contract)

9	  `docs/archive/commercial_v1_roadmap.md`)

11	
12	This document is the **product** view, written for a paying
13	external buyer. The previous draft (v0.1) framed hybrid_sim as an
14	Andes-internal acceleration tool. This rewrite repositions it as a
15	commercial Tier-2 EDA product competing with ARM Cycle Models,
16	Synopsys Imperas, and Wind River Simics-class hybrid offerings.
17	
18	---
19	
20	## 1. Executive Summary
21	
22	**Product name (working)**: Andes HybridSim
23	**Category**: Cycle-accurate hybrid simulator for RISC-V SoCs
24	**Cycle engine**: vsim (Verilator-derived, encrypted RTL pipeline)
25	**Fast engine**: QEMU 9.x with Andes plugin
26	**Target customer**: Andes IP licensees doing pre-silicon perf work
27	**Tier / price band**: Tier 2, $K-M/year per-seat or per-project
28	**Ship target**: Commercial v1.0 in ~12 months (engineering) +
29	6-12 months (encryption tooling) = ~18-24 months from today
30	**Differentiation**: only Tier-2 hybrid product with first-class
31	Andes IP (vendor CSRs, ACE, AndeStar V5 extensions) and zero FPGA
32	capex requirement
33	
34	**The one-line pitch**: "Cycle-exact RISC-V perf measurement on
35	real customer workloads, without an FPGA emulator or a multi-year
36	RTL learning curve."
37	
38	---
39	
40	## 2. Product Definition
41	
42	What the customer buys:
43	
44	| Component | Delivery | Purpose |
45	|---|---|---|
46	| `hsim` driver CLI | binary | orchestrates QEMU->vsim->QEMU handoff |
47	| QEMU (Andes fork) | binary + plugin SO | fast-forward engine, runs boring 99% |
48	| vsim cycle engine | **encrypted** binary | cycle-exact ROI measurement, RTL-derived but not RTL-recoverable |
49	| State transport library | linked into both | `hybrid_state_v1` wire format, mmap RAM |
50	| Trigger toolkit | linked + headers | magic-CSR, PC-watch, icount, SimPoint |
51	| Pipeline trace converter | binary | kanata / Clarity DB output |
52	| Reference flow | scripts + sample workloads | bare-metal kernel, Linux userspace, SPEC-class harness |
53	| License daemon | binary | per-seat / per-project enforcement |
54	| Documentation | PDF + HTML | user guide, ABI reference, integration guide |
55	| Support | contracted | tiered SLA |
56	
57	What the customer does NOT get:
58	- Raw Verilator C++ output (encrypted only)
59	- Andes RTL or microarch internals
60	- Source of the cycle engine
61	- QEMU source (binary only; upstream QEMU available separately)
62	
63	---
64	
65	## 3. Target Market & Buyer Personas
66	
67	### 3.1 Primary buyer: Andes IP licensee SoC integrator
68	
69	| Attribute | Profile |
70	|---|---|
71	| Company size | 50-2000 engineers; cannot justify $M+ ZeBu capex |
72	| Andes IP | one or more of AX25 / AX27 / AX45 / AX46 / D23v |
73	| Workload class | OS + userspace apps, AI inference kernels, networking dataplane |
74	| Pain | QEMU is too coarse; FPGA is too late; Alioth alone is too slow on real workloads |
75	| Buying authority | Engineering VP + IT procurement; budget cycle 6-12 months |
76	| Price tolerance | $20K-200K/seat/year, $200K-2M project license |
77	
78	### 3.2 Secondary buyer: research lab / university with industry tie-in
79	
80	| Attribute | Profile |
81	|---|---|
82	| Use case | Microarchitecture research, comparative perf studies |
83	| Procurement | Grant-funded; multi-year |
84	| Price tolerance | Academic discount tier; $5K-20K/seat/year |
85	| Value to Andes | Reference publications, conference visibility, talent pipeline |
86	
87	### 3.3 Personas at the buying customer
88	
89	| Role | What they care about |
90	|---|---|
91	| **SoC Architect** | accuracy vs RTL, modeling fidelity of vendor CSRs |
92	| **Perf Engineer** | wall-clock turnaround, SimPoint coverage, kanata output |
93	| **DV Engineer** | reproducibility, deterministic mode, log capture |

95	| **Legal / IP officer** | encryption guarantees, no RTL leakage, license terms |
96	| **IT / DevOps** | install footprint, license server, CI integration |

98	---
99	
100	## 4. Market Sizing & Opportunity
101	
102	Rough TAM estimate (top-down):
103	
104	- Andes IP active licensees: ~300 worldwide (public Andes 2025 figures)
105	- Fraction doing serious pre-silicon perf work: ~30% = ~90 accounts
106	- Fraction with ROI-style workloads (OS + hot kernel): ~60% = ~54 accounts
107	- Realistic 3-year capture rate: 20% = ~11 paying accounts
108	- Average deal size: $100K-500K/year
109	- Year-3 ARR target: $1.1M-5.5M
110	
111	Adjacent expansion:
112	- Non-Andes RISC-V vendors (SiFive, MIPS, Tenstorrent) could license
113	  the QEMU plugin + state transport without Andes-specific vendor
114	  CSRs. Out of scope for v1.0 but TAM-meaningful.
115	- Internal Andes engineering teams (~200 engineers) consume the
116	  product at internal cost; counts as cost avoidance vs ZeBu rental.
117	
118	---
119	
120	## 5. Competitive Positioning
121	
122	### 5.1 Competitive matrix (commercial Tier 2 focus)
123	
124	| Product | Vendor | Strength | Weakness vs HybridSim | Price band |
125	|---|---|---|---|---|
126	| ARM Cycle Models + Fast Models | ARM | mature, encrypted, CADI ecosystem | ARM-only ISA; no Andes IP; per-core not full cluster | $100K-1M/yr |
127	| Imperas (now Synopsys) | Synopsys | RISC-V leader; DPI-to-RTL | functional ISS + RTL bridge, not true hybrid; expensive | $200K-2M/yr |
128	| Wind River Simics + Hindsight | Wind River | full-system; large install base | not cycle-exact; weak RISC-V perf modeling | $50K-500K/yr |
129	| **Andes HybridSim** | **Andes** | **first-class Andes IP, $0 cycle-side capex, bundled SimPoint/kanata** | **alpha today; Andes ISA only** | **$K-M/yr** |
130	
131	Tier 1 (ZeBu/Palladium/Veloce) is explicitly not our competitive
132	target. They serve customers who already have $M+ FPGA capex.
133	
134	Tier 3 (gem5, Spike+DPI) is not our competitive target either.
135	Open-source pulls revenue to zero; we ship Andes IP correlation as
136	a paid product.
137	
138	### 5.2 The wedge
139	
140	Three things competitors do not deliver together:
141	
142	1. **First-class Andes IP modeling** - vendor CSRs, ACE, AndeStar V5,
143	   Andes platform (AE350-class) out of the box. ARM and Imperas
144	   require customer integration work; Wind River is functional-only.
145	2. **Zero FPGA capex** - runs on a Linux workstation. ZeBu/Palladium
146	   need a $M+ board.
147	3. **Bundled SimPoint + kanata + handoff orchestrator** - competitors
148	   sell these as separate add-ons or do not ship them at all.
149	
150	### 5.3 Honest losses
151	
152	- vsim cycle-side speed (5-50 KHz) is 1000-10000x slower than ZeBu
153	  emulator (10-100 MHz). For ROIs longer than ~1B cycles, ZeBu wins.
154	  Mitigation: SimPoint clustering shrinks effective ROI.
155	- ISA coverage is RISC-V Andes-only. ARM Cycle Models cover ARM
156	  ecosystem; Imperas covers broad RISC-V. Mitigation: deepen Andes
157	  IP support to make depth beat breadth.
158	- Maturity: ARM Cycle Models are 10+ years productized. Our v1.0
159	  is a fresh product. Mitigation: design-partner program before
160	  general availability.

164	## 6. Business Model

181	### 6.2 License enforcement
182	
183	- Network license daemon (FlexLM-class) per industry norm

189	### 6.3 Delivery channels

196	---

198	## 7. Market Requirements
199	
200	Numbered MRs for traceability into FRS.md. Each MR has a status
201	relative to v1.0 ship.
202	
203	### MR-A - Cycle-exact ROI measurement on customer workloads
204	
205	Customer provides their own ELF (closed source). HybridSim
206	fast-forwards in QEMU, switches to cycle engine at ROI, returns a
207	cycle figure correlated with RTL within an explicit error budget.
208	
209	- Acceptance: closed-source customer ELF round-trips; cycle figure
210	  agrees with fully-RTL baseline within 1% on the ROI window.
211	
212	### MR-B - Linux + userspace ROI
213	
214	Boot Linux, reach userspace hot loop, hand off to cycle engine,
215	measure, then drain.
216	
217	- Acceptance: at least 3 SPEC-class workloads under Linux userspace
218	  ship a cycle figure end-to-end.
219	
220	### MR-C - Whole-program estimate via SimPoint
221	
222	Long workload, no explicit ROI. SimPoint clustering picks
223	representative regions, cycle engine measures each, weighted
224	combine produces a whole-program estimate.
225	
226	- Acceptance: weighted estimate within 5-10% of fully-RTL on at
227	  least 3 SPEC-class workloads.
228	
229	### MR-D - Closed-source RTL protection (encryption)
230	
231	Cycle engine is RTL-derived (via Verilator) but the shipped binary
232	must not allow recovery of Andes RTL or microarch internals.
233	
234	- Acceptance: third-party reverse-engineering audit confirms no
235	  RTL recoverable from shipped binary; license + IP officer sign-off.

240	round-trip across the handoff with bit-exact semantics.

247	Customer can record kanata-format pipeline traces for the cycle

255	Architect changes a cycle-engine parameter (cache size, ROB depth),
256	rebuilds engine only, re-runs measurement against the same QEMU
257	checkpoint without re-running boot.
258	
259	- Acceptance: edit-rebuild-measure cycle under 5 minutes on a

262	### MR-H - Multi-hart support
263

265	through ACE.

268	  cycle figure within 1% of fully-RTL baseline.

287

292	- Acceptance: a deliberate state-corruption injection produces a

1	# ROADMAP - `andesim`: a multi-engine simulation framework
2	
3	> Scope of this file: building the `andesim` C++ framework. It supersedes the
4	> earlier "rewrite hsim (CoSIM-ready)" content in this file. It does NOT replace
5	> the repo-root `ROADMAP.md` (the master FR tracker). One feature per session;
6	> update each feature's **State** as you go.
7	
8	## Goal
9	
10	Turn the Python `hsim` driver into a single compiled C++20 executable named
11	**`andesim`** that is a *framework* hosting multiple simulator backends behind
12	one clear, self-describing interface - so QEMU (fast), Verilator (accurate),
13	Hybrid, and future simulators (alioth, sid) are all first-class, and new
14	Verilator builds can be added at runtime with no framework rebuild.
15	
16	## Vocabulary (three orthogonal concepts)
17	
18	- **Engine** = one simulator *process* the framework drives: `qemu`,
19	  `verilator:ax45mpv_premium`, `verilator:ax66_makatau`, later `alioth`, `sid`.
20	  This is the *pluggable* unit. Verilator has many engine instances (one per HW
21	  config); QEMU has one.
22	- **Model** = how chosen engines compose for a run:
23	  - `fast`     = QEMU alone (functional).
24	  - `accurate` = one Verilator alone, **pure - from reset, no QEMU** (cycle-accurate).
25	  - `hybrid`   = QEMU fast-forward -> Verilator measures the ROI (+ a trigger).
26	- **Trigger** = the ROI delimiter, used by `hybrid`: `marker` | `pc` | `icount` | `simpoint`.
27	
28	A run is `(model) x (engine) x (trigger)`.
29	
30	## Locked decisions
31	
32	- **Name:** the binary is `andesim` (the `hsim` "hybrid-sim" name retires).
33	- **Language: C++20**, existing clang++ toolchain; `#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"`
34	  directly (no hand-copied struct, no offsets).
35	- **Runtime = pure C++** (no Python, no shell on the run path). **Build and test
36	  infrastructure may stay shell/Python.**
37	- **Plugins are drop-in binaries, not linked libraries.** Engines are external
38	  processes; `andesim` is never recompiled to add one. No `dlopen`, no
39	  compiled-in engine list.
40	- **Discovery = scan + `--describe`.** The framework scans an engines directory
41	  and asks each binary to self-report its capabilities as JSON. A sidecar
42	  `<bin>.json` is the fallback for binaries that cannot add the flag. This is the
43	  hot-plug query mechanism.
44	- **Transparent passthrough for `fast`/`accurate`.** The framework parses only its
45	  selection flags; everything after `--` forwards verbatim to the engine. In these
46	  modes it inherits stdin/stdout/stderr, applies **no timeout**, and propagates the
47	  engine's exit code (exec-style). All native engine behavior is preserved - e.g.
48	  QEMU can hold a gdbstub and wait for a debugger. Users experience one simulator.
49	- **`accurate` = pure Verilator from reset, no QEMU.** vsim already supports this
50	  (default path; hybrid is gated by `--resume-from-qemu`). Cycles come from vsim's
51	  own output, not a drained state file.
52	- **No QEMU2 handback.** No gdbstub state-restore into a second QEMU. The `hybrid`
53	  cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` delta. The QEMU2 leg was removed from the repo
54	  entirely (`tests/e2e.sh` is a 2-phase harness now).
55	- **No CoSIM.** Dropped from this design.
56	
57	## Architecture (three layers)
58	
59	```
60	 andesim  (one C++20 binary; libc++ + include/hybrid/state_abi.h only)
61	   |
62	 [1] ENGINE REGISTRY  -- discover at runtime (the hot-plug seam)
63	   |     scan engines dir -> run `<bin> --describe` -> EngineDescriptor (JSON)
64	   |     qemu (built-in descriptor) | verilator:<cfg> (self-describe) | alioth/sid (self-describe)
65	   |
66	 [2] MODEL = composition  -- how chosen engines combine
67	   |     fast      = [ qemu ]                      transparent passthrough
68	   |     accurate  = [ verilator:<cfg> ]           transparent passthrough (from reset)
69	   |     hybrid    = [ qemu --ff--> verilator ]    orchestrated, + trigger
70	   |
71	 [3] PLAN EXECUTOR  -- (hybrid only) spawn legs, thread hybrid_state_v1, read mcycle
72	         run_plan(steps): per step -> registry invoke template -> spawn+timeout -> drain
73	```
74	
75	`fast`/`accurate` bypass layer [3] entirely (exec-passthrough). Only `hybrid`
76	orchestrates.
77	
78	## Engine interface (the contract alioth/sid follow)
79	
80	A simulator joins the framework by doing two things:
81	
82	**1. Self-describe.** Answer `--describe` with one JSON object:
83	
84	```json
85	{
86	  "id":       "verilator:ax45mpv_premium",
87	  "type":     "verilator",            // qemu | verilator | alioth | sid | ...
88	  "kind":     "cycle-accurate",       // functional | cycle-accurate
89	  "vlen":     512, "xlen": 64,        // optional HW params
90	  "triggers": ["marker","pc","icount"],  // ROI delimiters understood
91	  "roles":    ["standalone","accurate-leg"],  // standalone | fast-leg | accurate-leg
92	  "state":    ["resume","drain"],     // hybrid_state_v1 capabilities (omit if none)
93	  "invoke": {                         // argv prefix per role; {placeholders} filled by the framework
94	     "standalone":   ["{bin}", "{elf}"],
95	     "accurate-leg": ["{bin}", "--resume-from-qemu", "{state_in}",
96	                      "--handoff-out", "{state_out}", "--shared-mem-path", "{mmap}"]
97	  },
98	  "result":   "stderr:cycles"         // where the measurement is: stderr:<re> | state.mcycle
99	}
100	```
101	
102	**2. Speak the ABI for any role it claims.** Any engine listing `resume`/`drain`
103	in `state` must read/write `struct hybrid_state_v1` byte-for-byte
104	(`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`) and honor the shared-mmap convention. A
105	functional-only engine (`fast-leg`/`standalone`, no `state`) needs none of this.
106	
107	The framework needs **zero per-engine code** - everything it must know comes back
108	from `--describe`. Spec lives in `docs/engine_interface.md` (delivered in F2).
109

90	## Architecture
91	
92	### Two-Phase Handoff
93	
94	```
95	QEMU1 --(state file + shared mmap)--> vsim (resume + run ROI + drain)
96	```
97	
98	1. **QEMU plugin** (`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`) - TCG plugin. On the marker trigger (`slti x0, x0, 0x5A0`) or PC-trigger, drains QEMU's architectural state into a binary `hybrid_state_v1` struct written to `--outfile`.
99	2. **vsim handoff controller** (`src/hybrid/handoff_controller.hpp`) - Detects the trigger inside vsim, pauses the hart via DMI, then calls `ResumeDriver` to restore state.
100	3. **ResumeDriver** (`src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`) - Writes GPRs/FPRs/CSRs/V-state into the vsim hart via RISC-V Debug Module Abstract Commands and Program Buffer.
101	4. **StateDrain** (`src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp`) - On vsim exit trigger, reads back the full architectural state via DMI Abstract Commands into `hybrid_state_v1`. This is the end of the run: the cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` minus QEMU1's drained `mcycle`. The old QEMU2 resume leg was removed entirely.
102	
103	**CSR restore split**: `ResumeDriver` writes the CSRs the vsim phase can touch: `mstatus`, `mtvec`, `mscratch` (L23), `mepc`/`mcause`/`mtval`/`mie`/`mip` (L24), `mcycle`, `minstret`, `fcsr` (frm + sticky fflags, gated on `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`; L20), and the Andes machine-setup CSRs `mcache_ctl` (0x7CA) + `mmisc_ctl` (0x7D0) (L21). The cache pair matters for the cycle figure, not correctness: crt0 enables the L1 I/D caches via `mcache_ctl`, but that write runs on the cache-less functional engine, so without transporting it vsim resumes at the ROI with caches at their reset default (disabled) and the whole window runs uncached -- inflating the cycle count severalfold. All are tolerant writes: an engine without a given custom CSR mirrors the write as a no-op. In the trap-free ROI these writable M-mode CSRs are ordinary read/write state, so they round-trip fully: restored at resume, re-read at drain (`StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough`), and compared by `--verify` (`state_diff`). Two verify-side exceptions: `mip` is restored + re-read but NOT compared -- its pending bits are hardware/platform-driven (the timer bit tracks elapsed time, which advances differently in QEMU's functional clock vs vsim's cycle clock), so comparing it would false-positive; and `mtvec` is restored but not re-drained. The QEMU plugin still drains `medeleg`/`mideleg`/`satp` into `hybrid_state_v1`, but those are S-mode CSRs the default M-only engine (`ax45mpv_premium`, `NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1`) does not implement, so they are not restored -- they remain in `hybrid_state_v1` only as the drained record, deferred to the S/U-envelope work. The vsim phase is assumed trap-free, interrupt-free, and PMP-static; if a future workload needs traps or dynamic PMP inside the ROI, `ResumeDriver` must be extended.
104	
105	**Privilege (L6)**: the handoff carries the real privilege level. The plugin drains the gdbstub `priv` register, `ResumeDriver` read-modify-writes `dcsr.prv` before `dret` (and verifies the write took -- an M-mode-only RTL like the default `ax45mpv_premium`, `NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1`, WARL-pins the field, and the resume aborts with a pick-an-S/U-capable-engine error), and `StateDrain` reads `dcsr.prv` back at the exit halt. For S/U handoffs the producer's PMP block (64 `pmpaddr` + the 8 even `pmpcfg`) is also mirrored into the hart, because with PMP implemented and no matching entry every S/U access faults; M-mode handoffs keep PMP pass-through-only (L2). The `rt_priv_smode`/`rt_priv_umode` fixtures run on the S/U-capable `ax66_makatau` engine paired with QEMU `-cpu andes-ax66` (see `scripts/run_e2e.sh`); the ROI itself must still be trap-free, single-privilege, and paging-off (S-mode CSRs are not transported).
106	
107	### Trigger Modes
108	
109	The repo ships 4 switching modes, split by what they profile. The C++
110	`andesim` driver exposes the two kernel modes via `--trigger marker|pc`; the
111	two whole-program modes run through the Python golden (`hsim.py`).
112	
113	Kernel modes (measure one region you choose; `andesim --trigger marker|pc`):
114	- **marker mode** (default): Pattern-matches `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0` (entry) / `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1` (exit) at retire time. The markers are RISC-V HINTs (rd=x0 discards the result), i.e. architectural NOPs -- a marker binary also runs standalone on every engine and on silicon. Users get them from `<andesim/ROI.h>` (`andesim_ROI_begin()/end()`).
115	- **PC mode**: explicit boundary PCs passed as `--pc-start S --pc-end E` (symbol name or `0x` address) resolved at startup; marker insns are bypassed. Both args are required.
116	
117	Whole-program modes (sample by instruction count; Python golden `hsim.py`):
118	- **icount mode**: single boundary on each leg - plugin `icount=N` fast-forwards QEMU1, vsim `--hybrid-icount M` measures the window and drains. No markers, no warmup; for marker-less workloads. Removed as an `andesim --trigger` option; the measurement mechanism (plan `Trigger{kind:"icount"}` -> plugin `icount=` / vsim `--hybrid-icount`) is retained for SimPoint and driven directly by `./hsim.py run --mode icount`.
119	- **SimPoint-driven mode**: profile the run into slices (interval = insns per slice), cluster representative phases, measure each phase like icount, weight-combine into a whole-program cycle estimate. Drive via `./hsim.py run --mode simpoint` (or the equivalent `./hsim.py estimate`) -- Python golden only until the C++ port lands. The bbv-profile / archive / replay machinery are its stages, not separate modes.
120	
121	`./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker|pc` is the unified orchestrator for the kernel modes (`./hsim.py run --mode icount|simpoint` for the whole-program modes); `tests/e2e.sh` drives marker/pc internally. Each yields a cycle figure: kernel/window cycles = the vsim `mcycle` delta (`hybrid_state_v1::mcycle`); SimPoint reports the weight-combined `estimated_cycles`.
122	
123	### Shared ABI (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`)
124	
125	`hybrid_state_v1` is the binary wire format exchanged between the QEMU plugin and vsim. It holds: 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs, fcsr, M-mode CSRs (mstatus, mepc, etc.), PMP (64 pmpaddr + 16 pmpcfg), and the V extension block (vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, 32 vreg[], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr). `HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX=128` supports VLEN up to 1024 bits; the live width is the runtime `vlenb`, and a producer whose vlenb exceeds the ceiling refuses to drain instead of truncating (L11). Multi-byte fields are little-endian (native on RV64 + x86-64 host); the format is not endian-portable.
126	
127	Flags (`HYBRID_FLAG_RV64`, `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`, `HYBRID_FLAG_V`) gate which state blocks are live. The ABI struct is validated by `verilator/tests/hybrid/state_abi.test.cpp`.
128	
129	### V-State Transport
130	
131	V data registers (v0..v31) move through a scratch region in the shared mmap.
132	L26: that region is the mmap's TOP page, `v_scratch_gpa(ram_base, ram_size) =
133	ram_base + ram_size - HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES`, NOT a fixed address. The driver
134	maps one page more than `--mem-size` (`shm.cpp physical_mmap_bytes`), so the
135	scratch sits at `ram_base + --mem-size`, just above the program's RAM, where no
136	program layout can collide with it (`cmd_run` also rejects an ELF whose static
137	image would reach into it). `ResumeDriver`/`StateDrain` take the GPA as a
138	required-when-V argument (the simulator passes `v_scratch_gpa()`); a V handoff
139	with it unset throws. vsim drives the transfer via the Debug Module **Program
140	Buffer** while the hart is halted, so benchmark binaries issue no transport code:
141	- `stage_v_to_scratch` copies `hybrid_state_v1::vreg[]` into the scratch region
142	  before resume; `ResumeDriver` then sweeps `vle8.v v0..v31` from scratch into the
143	  regfile (`pb_v_data_sweep`, load=true).
144	- At drain, `StateDrain` sweeps `vse8.v v0..v31` from the regfile back to scratch
145	  (`pb_v_data_sweep`, load=false); `read_v_from_scratch` lifts the bytes into
146	  `hybrid_state_v1::vreg[]` (the drained handoff file; there is no QEMU2 ship step).
147	
148	Each sweep leads with `vsetvl` to e8/m1 (vl=vlenb), which also forces vstart=0 so
149	the unit-stride access covers the whole register. The scratch stride is the
150	compile-time `HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX` (wire-format per-register span), not the
151	runtime vlenb.
152	
153	V scalar CSR transport (vtype, vl, vstart, vxsat, vxrm, vcsr):
154	- **Tier A** (Abstract Commands): vstart, vxsat, vxrm, vcsr, mstatus.VS
155	- **Tier B** (Program Buffer): vtype + vl via `vsetvl x0, x5, x6` (direct CSR write to vtype sets vill; vl is read-only; only `vsetvl` restores both atomically)
156	
157	Restore order in `ResumeDriver::resume()` when `HYBRID_FLAG_V` is set:
158	1. `mstatus.VS` (enables V in the hart)
159	2. V-data reload sweep: `vsetvl` e8/m1 then `vle8.v v0..v31` from scratch in the
160	   Program Buffer. Runs BEFORE the architectural V-CSR restore (whose `vsetvl`
161	   overwrites the sweep's vtype/vl/vstart) and uses x5/x6/x7 as scratch.
162	3. `vsetvl x0, x5, x6` in Program Buffer (stages `vl` in x5, `vtype` in x6 via abstract GPR writes first)
163	4. `vstart` (AFTER vsetvl: vsetvl resets vstart to 0)
164	5. `vxsat`, `vxrm`, `vcsr`
165	6. GPR loop (overwrites the x5/x6/x7 scratch - safe now)
166

### Trigger Modes

The repo ships 4 switching modes, split by what they profile. The C++
`andesim` driver exposes the two kernel modes via `--trigger marker|pc`; the
two whole-program modes run through the Python golden (`hsim.py`).

Kernel modes (measure one region you choose; `andesim --trigger marker|pc`):
- **marker mode** (default): Pattern-matches `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0` (entry) / `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1` (exit) at retire time. The markers are RISC-V HINTs (rd=x0 discards the result), i.e. architectural NOPs -- a marker binary also runs standalone on every engine and on silicon. Users get them from `<andesim/ROI.h>` (`andesim_ROI_begin()/end()`).
- **PC mode**: explicit boundary PCs passed as `--pc-start S --pc-end E` (symbol name or `0x` address) resolved at startup; marker insns are bypassed. Both args are required.

Whole-program modes (sample by instruction count; Python golden `hsim.py`):
- **icount mode**: single boundary on each leg - plugin `icount=N` fast-forwards QEMU1, vsim `--hybrid-icount M` measures the window and drains. No markers, no warmup; for marker-less workloads. Removed as an `andesim --trigger` option; the measurement mechanism (plan `Trigger{kind:"icount"}` -> plugin `icount=` / vsim `--hybrid-icount`) is retained for SimPoint and driven directly by `./hsim.py run --mode icount`.
- **SimPoint-driven mode**: profile the run into slices (interval = insns per slice), cluster representative phases, measure each phase like icount, weight-combine into a whole-program cycle estimate. Drive via `./hsim.py run --mode simpoint` (or the equivalent `./hsim.py estimate`) -- Python golden only until the C++ port lands. The bbv-profile / archive / replay machinery are its stages, not separate modes.

`./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker|pc` is the unified orchestrator for the kernel modes (`./hsim.py run --mode icount|simpoint` for the whole-program modes); `tests/e2e.sh` drives marker/pc internally. Each yields a cycle figure: kernel/window cycles = the vsim `mcycle` delta (`hybrid_state_v1::mcycle`); SimPoint reports the weight-combined `estimated_cycles`.
